transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Um, hello. Well... I suppose I'm here because I keep getting up when I'm supposed to be sitting down. 

Like during staff meetings, or just at dinner. Everyone else is seated, and I just... I'll suddenly get up to refill my coffee, or check a handout, or just walk to the back of the room. Even when nothing is really urgent. So... yes, that's why.
Has this difficulty staying seated been present since you were a child, or is it a more recent change?

Well... no, it's not a recent change. I suppose it's been this way since I was a girl. 

My old report cards usually said I was bright, but... that I couldn't stay in my seat. Or wait my turn. And my mother, she used to joke that I wore a path in the floor between my desk and the pencil sharpener before I was ten. So... yes. Since childhood.
Do you often find it difficult to maintain your focus or sustain attention when working on tasks?

Um... no. I don't think so. I can focus on my work just fine. I mean, I get things done when I need to, like grading or planning. I haven't really noticed any... trouble with paying attention. It's really just what I mentioned before.
Do you often feel restless inside, as if you are driven by a motor and constantly need to be on the go?

Um... I suppose so. I just... keep busy. 

Since the house got quieter, after my youngest left for college, I just find myself moving from one thing to the next. I'll go from lesson planning to the laundry, to... softball practice, or chopping food for a community event. I don't really pause much. Even on the nights I promise myself I'm just going to sit and rest... I don't. So... yes. I suppose I am always on the go.
Do you find yourself constantly worrying about many everyday things, to the point that it feels hard to control?
No... not really. I mean, I have normal worries, I suppose. Just the usual things. But I wouldn't say it's hard to control. I just... stay busy instead of worrying.
